audit.whatIsWrong: The entry calls Thundering Smash (Q) a dash/leap and calls Sky Splitter (E) a stun. Both are wrong: Q is a move-speed ramp that stuns the first enemy he Attacks, E is a ranged damage+slow that shields him if he stands in it. Volibear has no dash until Stormbringer (R).
audit.why: Telling a Teemo to 'bait the Q leap and let him overshoot' teaches a losing habit — you cannot make a speed-ramp overshoot. And waiting for an 'E stun' that does not exist means the real stun (Q) lands unpunished.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash (Q) ramps his move speed toward you and stuns on his next attack; Sky Splitter (E) is the 1200-range slow + self-shield; Stormbringer (R) is his only leap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere says which of Volibear's damage sources Blind actually stops. The entry claims Blinding Dart 'negates his only early-trade tool'.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul (W) is a targeted cast on a flat 5s cooldown that applies on-hit effects and heals him. Blind stops basic attacks; it does not stop a spell cast. A Teemo who blinds and then stands in 325 range eats the full bite and the heal.
audit.corrected: Blind erases his autos and his passive on-hit; it does nothing to Frenzied Maul. Leaving his 325-unit W range is what denies the bite and the heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no real numbers — just 'His engage. Blind + kite it.'
audit.why: The exploitable windows are concrete: Thundering Smash is 12s at rank 1 falling to 10s at rank 5, Sky Splitter is a flat 16s, Frenzied Maul is a flat 5s and effectively always up. Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank, so your blind cycles faster than his stun does.
audit.corrected: Q 12s->10s, W 5s, E 16s, R 160/135/110. Your Q is 7s flat — you get roughly two blinds per Thundering Smash.

audit.why: Frenzied Maul heals him on the second cast against the same target, so the existing Oblivion Orb / anti-heal emphasis is right and the _missing-interactions needs-antiheal flag is already satisfied by the entry's anti-heal lines.
Stormbringer disabling towers near his landing point is stated correctly in spikes[2] and whys[4] and is confirmed by Riot's own text.

edits.before: Volibear's only Level 1 move is walking up to auto you — Blinding Shot deletes that plan entirely, so open Q and set the poke tone immediately. He cannot threaten you without his empowered Q dash, and that comes at Level 2; when he reaches Level 2, bait the Q leap by retreating with W, let him overshoot, then turn back and re-stack Toxic Shot poison while he is committed to a dead-end gap-close. His W bite deals damage and heals but it requires him to be in melee range first — deny him that range and the heal never happens.
edits.after: Volibear's only Level 1 move is walking up to auto you — Blinding Dart deletes that plan entirely, so open Q and set the poke tone immediately. Thundering Smash arrives at Level 2 and is a speed ramp, not a leap: he cannot overshoot you, so you beat it by pre-moving with W before he closes rather than by side-stepping on reaction. His W Frenzied Maul is a cast, not an auto — Blind never stops the bite or the heal — but it only reaches 325 units, so deny him that range and neither half of it ever happens.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your controlling window: max Q first means every Blind lasts long enough to absorb his entire trade pattern, and shrooms placed at the tribush and river bush mean he cannot rotate or all-in without triggering slow plus a poison stack before the fight even starts. Keep him at roughly 60-70 percent HP through sustained Toxic Shot pokes so he cannot safely hard commit. At Level 6 treat the lane with respect — his R disables the tower and his E stun is what actually kills you, not the autos you are already Blinding, so shroom the base of your tower and the jungle entrance behind your lane before he hits 6.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your controlling window: max Q first means every Blind lasts long enough to absorb his entire trade pattern, and shrooms placed at the tribush and river bush mean he cannot rotate or all-in without triggering slow plus a poison stack before the fight even starts. Keep him at roughly 60-70 percent HP through sustained Toxic Shot pokes so he cannot safely hard commit. At Level 6 treat the lane with respect — his R disables the tower and his Q stun into a flat-5-second Frenzied Maul is what actually kills you, not the autos you are already Blinding, so shroom the base of your tower and the jungle entrance behind your lane before he hits 6.

edits.before: From 6 the shroom net makes his half of the map hostile terrain. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Volibear's ultimate changes the math too.

notes: Volibear's Q is a move-speed ramp with a stun on his next attack, not a dash — the old text repeatedly told the reader to bait a leap that does not exist. His E is a slow+shield, not a stun. Whether Blind causes Thundering Smash's stun-attack to whiff is not answerable from the kit file (needsResearch is empty), so no claim is made either way; the edits stay on the safe side by pointing at Frenzied Maul, which is unambiguously a cast.
